content:
Hello everyone!

I’m new to Lean and have some familiarity with Zulip. I’m interested in formalizing results about (log) del Pezzo surfaces. I understand that mathlib already has a substantial amount of algebraic geometry formalized.

If anyone is already working on a similar project, I’d be very happy to learn and collaborate. Any advice, suggestions, or pointers on where to start would be very welcome!

It has a substantial amount of facts about derived categories and schemes but I'm not sure it has the canonical divisor yet, and if certainly doesn't have all the basic facts about surfaces (it doesn't even have Rienann Roch for curves), it has essentially nothing about coherent sheaves, and it's probably already a challenge to define a Del Pezzo surface.

@Kevin Buzzard Thanks. I was thinking again about this after the recent OpenAI mathematics release.

I had a look at their Lean repository, and it seems there is now quite a bit more algebraic geometry available, also in Mathlib, especially around sheaves and quasi-coherent sheaves. But I still don't see the surface theory you mentioned before: canonical divisors, intersection theory, Riemann–Roch, etc.

Do you think the situation has improved enough that there is now a reasonable entry point for this project?

I was also wondering what the best practical way is to check what has already been formalized in Lean, including projects outside Mathlib.

My current thought is to start with a very small Mathlib-based project, maybe first with exceptional collections on the categorical side, rather than trying to fork a large repository. Does that sound sensible?
